To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the health of students in a school building with moisture damage was improved after comprehensive repair of the moisture damage.
the moisture damage repairs had a positive impact on the health of the students, but that the effect was not as strong as the cross-sectional design might have suggested.
the health symptoms among the students improved in the cross-sectional analysis, but not in the longitudinal analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of moisture damage and its repairs in school buildings on students’ health.
the reversibility of the health effect of moisture damage and the effectiveness of the repairs.
the long-term effects of moisture damage and its repairs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the repairs had a positive effect on the health of the school population.
the repairs were effective in preventing new cases of symptoms among the exposed population but not in reversing the symptoms among the already symptomatic individuals.
the repairs were effective in the sense that the situation was significantly improved among the cross-sectional populations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the moisture damage repairs had a positive effect on health symptoms among students, but the effect was not so strong as to eliminate symptoms among the students who were exposed to the moisture damage before the repairs.
moisture damage repairs in schools are a cost-effective measure to reduce the risk for students’ health symptoms.
moisture repairs are effective in the sense that they stop new cases of symptoms, but the reversibility of the symptoms among the group who have experienced symptoms is not so obvious.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of moisture repairs on health symptoms may not be as straightforward as expected.
it is not sufficient to measure the effect of an intervention only by the change in the prevalence of symptoms among the population.
the effects of moisture damage interventions on the exposed population may be underestimated in cross-sectional analyses.
